headline: Adjusted profit surges as FTC charge dents GAAP earnings
summary_short: Corpay's Q2 revenue rose 21% y/y to $1,338.8M with 10% organic growth, but GAAP net income fell 13% to $248.3M after a $100M preliminary FTC settlement charge; adjusted EBITDA rose 24% to $767.2M and adjusted diluted EPS grew 36% to $7.00.
summary_long: Revenue grew 21% y/y to $1,338.8M (10% organic, a fifth straight quarter of double-digit organic growth), led by Corporate Payments (+42% GAAP, +16% organic, including the Alpha acquisition). GAAP net income fell 13% to $248.3M and diluted EPS fell 7% to $3.70, both dragged by a $100 million preliminary FTC settlement charge. Adjusted EBITDA rose 24% to $767.2M and adjusted diluted EPS grew 36% to $7.00. The company repurchased $321M of stock, refinanced its debt (revolver upsized to $3.7B, 2.55x leverage), and raised full-year 2026 revenue, net income and adjusted EPS guidance; Q3 2026 revenue is guided to ~$1.355B and adjusted diluted EPS to ~$7.15 at the midpoint.

drivers.explanation: CEO called the quarter 'excellent,' citing 21% revenue growth and a fifth consecutive quarter of double-digit organic growth from the company's continued rotation into corporate payments and spend management.

Growth was led by Corporate Payments (+42% reported, +16% organic, including the Alpha acquisition) and Vehicle Payments (+13%), with reported growth also aided by fuel price, spread and FX tailwinds versus the macro-adjusted figure.

GAAP net income and EPS fell y/y because the company recorded a $100 million charge for a preliminary settlement with the FTC's Bureau of Consumer Protection, subject to its customary approval process, expected to conclude later this year.

Adjusted EBITDA and its margin (57.3% vs 56.3%) rose on segment revenue growth, including the Alpha acquisition within Corporate Payments and continued sequential organic improvement in Lodging Payments.

Adjusted diluted EPS grew faster than adjusted net income (36% vs 27%) partly because diluted share count fell to 66.3M from 71.4M after the company repurchased 1 million shares for $321 million in the quarter.
